## Conceptual core: what a page field is

A **page field** is a pivot field that controls *which subset* of the source data is shown in the body of the pivot table. End users see it as a dropdown at the top of the rendered pivot in Excel — selecting a value filters the rows/columns the pivot summarizes.

Two important behaviors:
- **Single-select** (default): only one page item is visible; the pivot shows one subset at a time.
- **Multi-select**: multiple page items can be checked simultaneously; the pivot shows the union of the selected subsets.

The pivot field that drives this filter is registered as `PivotFieldType.Page` (as opposed to Row, Column, or Data).

## CRITICAL — Required using directives

The pivot types live in **`Aspose.Cells.Pivot`**. Every C# example MUST start with:

```csharp
using System;
using Aspose.Cells;
using Aspose.Cells.Pivot;
```

## CRITICAL — Exact API reference

| API | Purpose |
|-----|---------|
| `PivotTable.AddFieldToArea(PivotFieldType.Page, "fieldName")` | Add a field to the page area using its source-column name. The most common, high-level API. |
| `PivotTable.PageFields.Add(PivotField)` | Add an existing `PivotField` instance to the page area. Useful when you already have a `PivotField` object reference or want to add the same field to multiple areas. |
| `PivotTable.PageFields[int index]` | Access a registered page field by index. |
| `PivotField.CurrentPageItem` | (Single-select) `int` index of the currently visible item. Assign a specific item index to filter, or assign the special "all items" value to show every item. |
| `PivotField.IsMultipleItemSelectionAllowed` | (Multi-select) `bool` — set to `true` to enable the multi-select checkbox UI in Excel; necessary to use `PivotField.HideItem` / `PivotItem.IsHidden`. |
| `PivotField.PivotItems` | `PivotItemCollection` — the list of `PivotItem` objects for this page field. |
| `PivotItem.IsHidden` | `bool` — set to `true` to hide an item from the multi-select list; `false` to make it visible. **At least one item must remain visible (`IsHidden == false`).** |
| `PivotItem.GetStringValue()` | Returns the source-data string the item represents (e.g. "2020", "grape"). |
| Special "all items" value for `CurrentPageItem` | The integer `0x7FFD` (decimal 32765) selects ALL items — equivalent to clearing the page filter. Use this when you want to show everything. |

## Required coverage — 5 code scenarios

### 1. Add a page field (TWO code blocks — both fully runnable, both start from scratch)

#### 1a. High-level: `PivotTable.AddFieldToArea(PivotFieldType.Page, "fieldName")`

Complete self-contained example: build a workbook with Fruit/Year/Amount data (9 rows), add a pivot at `E3`, assign Fruit→Row, Amount→Data, then add a Year→Page field via `AddFieldToArea`, save as `output.xlsx`. Use the standard sample data shape that every other article in this guide uses.

#### 1b. Low-level: `PageFields.Add(PivotField)`

Same data layout and pivot table as 1a. Show that you can also obtain a `PivotField` (e.g. by calling `pivotTable.BaseFields["Year"]`) and pass it to `pageFields.Add(...)`. The result is functionally identical to 1a.

### 2. Single-select filtering (TWO code blocks — both reference the pivot table from Scenario 1a)

#### 2a. Show ALL items (clear the page filter)
```csharp
// (setup as in Scenario 1a, summarized in a code comment)
pivotTable.PageFields[0].CurrentPageItem = 0x7FFD; // all items
workbook.Save("output.xlsx");
```
Note the magic number `0x7FFD` and add an inline comment explaining it is the special value for "all items".

#### 2b. Show only ONE specific item
```csharp
// (setup as in Scenario 1a)
pivotTable.PageFields[0].CurrentPageItem = 1; // 2nd item (e.g. "2021")
workbook.Save("output.xlsx");
```
Mention that this is just an index into the page field's items, so "1" picks the second item after sorting.

### 3. Multi-select filtering (ONE code block — references Scenario 1a)

Single code block with TWO clearly labeled parts.

#### Header/setup
```csharp
// (setup as in Scenario 1a, summarized in a code comment)
// — including: enable multi-select on the page field
pivotTable.PageFields[0].IsMultipleItemSelectionAllowed = true;
```

#### Part A — select ALL items
Use the **range loop** that hides every item WITHOUT setting them all to hidden — i.e. set every `pivotItems[i].IsHidden = false`:
```csharp
PivotItemCollection pivotItems = pivotTable.PageFields[0].PivotItems;
for (int i = 0; i < pivotItems.Count; i++)
{
    pivotItems[i].IsHidden = false;
}
```

#### Part B — select a few specific items by source value
Use the `switch` on `pivotItems[i].GetStringValue()` to whitelist, default to hidden:
```csharp
for (int i = 0; i < pivotItems.Count; i++)
{
    switch (pivotItems[i].GetStringValue())
    {
        case "2020":
        case "grape":
        case "blueberry":
            pivotItems[i].IsHidden = false;
            break;
        default:
            pivotItems[i].IsHidden = true;
            break;
    }
}
workbook.Save("output.xlsx");
```

**Critical note in the article body**: at least one `PivotItem` MUST stay visible (`IsHidden == false`). Hiding all items crashes Excel or leaves a blank pivot. The C# code's `default` branch is safe because the source data always has at least one of the listed items, but readers should NOT write code like `all -> hidden` blindly.
